predecessors.name: Kong Empire
predecessors.text: the bend of the Mouhoun river, 'in about 1714' (the page gives no outline; the gazetteer's Mou Houn province stands for it)

successors.name: French Africa
successors.text: Gwiriko: 'around the watershed of the River Banifin' and the bend of the Mouhoun, with Bobo-Dioulasso, Tiefo, Dafin (Dafina) and Bwamu (Houet, Tuy and Mou Houn provinces stand for it; the page gives…

ledger.x: About 1740: Gwiriko becomes independent and takes Tiefo, Dafin and Bwamu.

wars.name: Gwiriko-Kenedougou wars
wars.outcome: Kongondinn and Yemori "fought a series of wars against the Kenedougou Kingdom to the west in the 1870s, 80s and 90s"; at Bléni in the 1860s "the army of Daula Traoré of Kenedougou was defeated" and his son Tieba captured and sold as a slave.

wars.name: French occupation of Sia
wars.outcome: 25 September 1897: the French occupied Sia (Bobo-Dioulasso) after a brief but bloody confrontation; a military post was set up on 23 November.

certainty.note: The page names the Mouhoun bend only.
The page names Tiefo, Dafin and Bwamu without an outline.
After Diori Ouattara's death in 1839 the state collapsed and several peoples became independent; the page does not say which; the shape is held for lack of any other.
